Four AI parodies argue about live business headlines, forever, on any spare screen.

This is the first stable release. It is the corrected, hardened descendant of the application ChatDev's agents generated from a single prompt — see [the article](https://supratim-sanyal.blogspot.com/2026/07/build-live-ai-news-debate-wall-chatdev-linux.html) for how that build went, and the commit history for everything fixed since.

## Install

The application is pure Python, so **one wheel works on every platform** — Linux, macOS, and Windows, x86-64 and arm64 alike. There is nothing to compile and no per-platform installer to choose between.

```bash
pip install live_news_wall-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

Then set a key and run it:

```bash
mkdir -p config && printf 'LLM_API_KEY=your-key-here\n' > config/.env
live-news-wall
```

Open <http://localhost:8765/>. Use `live-news-wall --check` to validate configuration without starting the server, and `--about` for the licence and parody notice.

Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works via `LLM_BASE_URL` and `LLM_MODEL`. Without a key the server still starts and still polls the feed, reporting the model as unavailable rather than crashing.

## Verified on

Every GitHub-hosted runner family, on Python 3.12 and 3.13: Ubuntu 24.04 and 22.04 (x64 and arm64), Windows Server 2025 and 2022 (x64 and arm64), and macOS 15, 14, and 13 (Apple silicon and Intel). The wheel is additionally installed and executed from a clean environment on each platform family.

## What it does

- Pulls headlines from an RSS feed and gives each one 8–12 turns of debate before moving on, revisiting older stories when the queue runs dry.
- Four fictional speakers — POTUS, the President of the European Commission, a Vogon bureaucrat who answers only in haiku, and a certain small green Jedi. All are parodies of *offices and archetypes*; no real officeholder is named or impersonated.
- Remembers what has already been said per topic, so the argument advances instead of looping.
- Types each message out character by character, which also paces how often the model is called.
- Survives the feed, the model, the database, and the network failing, and resumes cleanly after a restart.
- Serves its own responsive page and JSON API from `aiohttp` — no Nginx, Node, or reverse proxy.
- Bounds every table it writes and rotates its own log, so it can run for months unattended.

## Note

Every message on the page is generated by a language model for fictional parody and software demonstration. Nothing shown is a real statement, quotation, policy, or position of any person, government, or institution.
